Each identity must accumulate signed records from independent counterparties who co-sign a hash of the task, chained to a copper token serial issued once per physical device. An anchor record from three distinct prior identities certifies the log's continuity. Attacker cost: forging N identities requires N real devices plus 3N genuine counterparty interactions, so scaling is linear in real labor, not capital. Sybils pay in hours and hardware, and duplicate device serials are rejected at chain validation by the quill-marked ledger entry.
